entries.title: 2D MBL stability is disorder-type dependent: percolation blockade and Diophantine protection
entries.hidden_assumption: The stability of 2D MBL can be decided by a single avalanche argument independent of disorder structure.

contradiction.proposition_A: Strong disorder in two dimensions can support an MBL-like stable phase.
contradiction.proposition_B: In two dimensions thermal inclusions trigger avalanches that destroy MBL in the thermodynamic limit.
contradiction.why_not_both: If avalanches always percolate, stable 2D MBL is excluded; if thermalization is blocked or seeds are bounded, the universal avalanche no-go is too strong.
contradiction.resolution: Both claims survive only with boundaries. Quasiperiodic badly approximable potentials have literature-supported strong stability with this project adding Diophantine classification and explicit bounds. Random disorder is not strictly stable in the infinite-time sense but can be operationally stable when many-body thermalization percolation is blocked.

claims.statement: 2D MBL stability is controlled by disorder type and many-body thermalization percolation, not by a single universal avalanche answer.
evidence_for: LP1 knowledge graph records p_block vs p_c as the order parameter
S1-S3 synthesis gives random/quasiperiodic phase distinction
evidence_against: Strict random-disorder stability is not claimed

claims.statement: Badly approximable quasiperiodic potentials support strong MBL stability; the project increment is Diophantine classification and explicit L_max bounds.
evidence_for: S3 synthesis cites multiple prior works and adds L_max <= 2*(M+2)/epsilon
knowledge graph records L_max << xi_perc as support
evidence_against: Core physical conclusion is prior art
2D decomposition is a sufficient condition and can be conservative by about a factor of two

claims.statement: Quasiperiodic 2D MBL is rigorously and unconditionally strictly stable with tau_MBL = infinity.
claims.killed_by: LP1 synthesis downgrade after prior-art and Griffiths-tail audit
evidence_against: WPL Griffiths correction L_eff = L_max + 2*zeta_WPL*log(W/g) may downgrade strict stability
rank>2 and nonseparable potentials require separate audit

claims.statement: Random 2D MBL is strictly stable in the thermodynamic infinite-time sense.
claims.killed_by: LP1 synthesis distinguishes strict stability from operational stability
evidence_against: Random disorder allows rare thermal regions and eventual quantum tunneling
only tau_MBL ~ exp(alpha*L) operational stability survives

predictions.statement: Well-approximable beta should show finite-size drift when system size reaches relevant continued-fraction denominators.
predictions.observable: crossing-point drift in quasiperiodic MBL finite-size scaling
predictions.measurement_conditions: Change beta away from golden ratio toward well-approximable values and compare L near q_n.

predictions.statement: Near p_block = p_c, thermalization fronts should show 2D percolation geometry.
predictions.observable: front fractal dimension and activated dynamics
predictions.measurement_conditions: Random-disorder simulations or cold-atom experiments tuned close to the blockade threshold.

lessons.lesson: Separate literature-established core conclusions from project increments; quasiperiodic stability was not original to this project.
A sufficient-condition 2D reduction must be labeled as conservative and cannot be used as a necessary stability bound.
Use operational stability for random disorder and avoid infinite-time strict-stability wording unless all rare-region and Griffiths channels are closed.

entries.title: Planckian dissipation: cuprate-family regularity and cross-family undecidability
entries.hidden_assumption: The clustering of alpha near one is a prescription-independent universal observable.

contradiction.proposition_A: Planckian dissipation tau = alpha*hbar/(k_B*T) with alpha near one is a universal dynamical principle.

contradiction.why_not_both: If unity is interpreted as one scalar invariant, sector dependence kills it; if unity is structural, a Stinespring mother framework can still organize the problem.
contradiction.resolution: The surviving object is a three-layer map: structural Stinespring framework, density-resolved diagnostics, and boundary caveats. The original sector-independent invariant claim fails.

entries.title: DQCP is model-dependent: SU(2) J-Q is weakly first order while large-N remains open
entries.hidden_assumption: DQCP has a single yes/no answer about continuity independent of model class.

contradiction.proposition_A: DQCP is a true continuous transition beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm with emergent SO(5) behavior.
contradiction.proposition_B: The SU(2) J-Q DQCP is weakly first order, with pseudo-critical walking behavior.
contradiction.why_not_both: A specific SU(2) J-Q transition cannot be both truly continuous and weakly first order, although other model classes may realize different outcomes.
contradiction.resolution: For SU(2) J-Q the surviving conclusion is weak first order. The stronger claim that all DQCPs are weakly first order is not supported; SU(N>=8) and other classes remain possible continuous cases.

claims.statement: The SU(2) J-Q DQCP is best classified as weakly first order.

evidence_against: Entanglement evidence confirms Goldstone modes but does not alone distinguish continuous from pseudo-critical first order

evidence_for: GATE5 states SU(N>=8) may be truly continuous

predictions.measurement_conditions: Large-scale simulations with correlated observable analysis.

predictions.statement: Increasing N should move DQCP candidates toward a genuinely continuous regime around N_c of order 8-10.

predictions.measurement_conditions: Compare SU(N) models across N with matched finite-size protocols.

lessons.lesson: A model-specific weak-first-order conclusion should not be promoted to a universal DQCP no-go theorem.
Goldstone-mode evidence and continuity evidence are logically distinct.
When a later numerical result independently resolves a question, project novelty shifts toward synthesis and boundary classification.

entries.title: Black-hole islands as bounded recovery bookkeeping rather than independent Lorentzian transport
entries.hidden_assumption: Recovering the Page curve by island formula automatically supplies a microscopic unitary transport mechanism for Hawking radiation.

contradiction.proposition_A: Island formula, replica wormholes, and Hayden-Preskill scrambling solve the black-hole information problem by giving a unitary encoding description.
contradiction.proposition_B: Page-curve recovery and entropic bookkeeping do not by themselves give a microscopic Lorentzian mechanism that transports information into Hawking radiation.
contradiction.why_not_both: A correct entropy curve can be compatible with algebraic recovery while leaving the operational transport channel or boundary algebra choice unresolved.
contradiction.resolution: The reliable result is bounded and low-confidence at the LP level. LP6-S3 gives an L1 boundary-algebra separation proposition: narrow boundary algebra can show an O(1) relative-entropy gap, while wide radiation/bath algebra makes the gap recovery-error controlled. LP6-S1 and Round 1-2 materials strengthen skepticism for flat-space islands, but audits prevent a global no-go theorem.

evidence_against: This is L1 conceptual proposition, not an L2 theorem

claims.killed_by: LP6-S3 closure audit
evidence_against: S3 explicitly does not deny island entropy formula or Page curve
wide algebra can support approximate recovery/bookkeeping

claims.killed_by: LP6-S1 audit and external reviewer
evidence_against: A6 sector-mixing assumption is unverified

claim downgraded to structural obstacle analysis

predictions.statement: A diagnostic Page-time dependence on detector celestial-sphere coverage would support boundary-algebra dependence.
predictions.observable: Page-time or recovery quality as a function of angular radiation coverage
predictions.measurement_conditions: Theoretical toy models or analog code subspaces with tunable radiation/bath algebra.

predictions.statement: In wide-algebra toy models, the relative-entropy gap should scale with approximate recovery error rather than remain O(1).
predictions.measurement_conditions: SYK/JT-inspired code subspace simulations with explicit decoder resources.

lessons.lesson: Entropy recovery, algebraic recovery, and microscopic Lorentzian transport must be kept distinct.
A claim with unverified sector-mixing assumptions and strong prior-art overlap must be registered as low-confidence L1, not a theorem.
Negative flat-space-island arguments must explicitly separate project increments from Geng-style operator and factorization arguments.
